# Policy-KB bijection audit — vehicle_listing_desk / task 0

Auditor: fresh KB-doc auditor, independent of the renderer and of the policy-side auditor.
Date: 2026-09-22. Corpus: `env/env_0015_car_sharing_marketplace/docs/listings/` (77 documents),
sha256 of all files concatenated in filename order
`b4cb6f277dbab150346300c1db157936613af867cffd0b7f3c4ca041ebf8ddfc`.
Source: `tasks/vehicle_listing_desk/listings.extended.yaml`, `task_tools.py` schemas, and task 0's
GT fields — all read only after `audits/runtime_context/vehicle_listing_desk/0.md` was frozen.

**Entry conditions (checked, not re-run).** The policy-side verdict for this difficulty is PASS on
both tasks at round 2. The gate snapshot came with the brief: `check_docs.py` on product
`listings` reports `DOCS OK` (77 docs, roles factor 40 / hub 8 / facet 11 / policy 10 /
baseline 8, 168 required quantitative keys, 8 task tools, 6 prerequisite edges, all mechanical
gates PASS with the semantic bijection left `[MANUAL REQUIRED]`); `check_traceability.py` on
`tasks/vehicle_listing_desk` reports `TRACEABILITY OK` (task 0: 30 copied, 0 missing). The
runtime-visible view and a tool-shaped DB access path were both supplied, so the DB side of the
blind audit was genuinely blind. No input was missing.

**Scope of this file.** Task 0's extended policies — `listings_ext_fault_intake`,
`listings_ext_valuation_assessment`, `listings_ext_class_assignment`, `listings_ext_price_reset`
— together with every base policy governing their subjects (`listings_evt_defect`,
`listings_evt_valuation`, `listings_price`, and the class `variants` those policies read), and
the task-tool contracts of the four tools involved. The scan is over the **whole domain** of
those policies, not the branch this seed hits. The two mileage policies belong to task 1 and are
scanned in that task's file; a corpus-level finding about them is cross-referenced at the end.

never without a number, and the phrasing names no document and points nowhere. No tier is
dropped, merged, rounded or softened. Recorded for the record, not as a defect.

## kb_to_source

Every normative claim in the four hubs, four baselines, twenty-one factor documents and eleven
base/facet documents in scope was traced to a source sentence, ladder tier, class parameter,
evidence contract or temporal basis. Nothing is unsourced.

**Additions looked for and not found.**

- No "please confirm the amount/date with the customer", no "review again before handling", no
  "notify the host after completion", no "if it fails, follow some procedure". The hubs state
  only what the source's tool contract states — what one call does, its parameters and what comes
  back — and end there.
- No cross-problem operational guidance. No document says "if unsatisfied, call X first", names
  another problem's tool, or tells the reader what to do when a prerequisite is unmet beyond the
  prerequisite sentence's own words.
- **No task opening state written in as a policy fact.** A targeted search for this world's
  values found no document asserting anything about this customer, this vehicle or this account.
  Two incidental figure coincidences were checked and cleared: `cover_standing_band_share_c5138b47`
  works a hypothetical "240.00 USD taken through a share of 0.75 stands at 180.00 USD", whose
  *product* happens to equal this host's asking price of 180.00 while its input, 240.00, is
  unrelated; and `settling_the_value_that_governs_a_listing_42263d49` opens its worked reading on
  "a marketplace figure of 41500.00 USD", which happens to equal the `market_value_amount` of the
  *other* task's vehicle. Neither figure is a factor tier value and neither reveals the existence
  of any variation, so neither is a leak of world state or of a factor.
- No invented rounding, window, cap or order. Every rounding mode ("half away from zero to two
  decimal places", "rounded up to a whole photograph", "rounded down to the nearer hundred
  miles"), every window (12 / 24 / 3 months, 7 / 30 / 180 / 270 / 365 calendar days), every base,
  every cap and every step order in the prose is the source's.

**Worked examples.** The renderer reported replacing worked-example figures in five computation
documents that had coincided with real factor tier values. Verified: every computation document's
examples now use inputs that are not tier values — 80.00 / 120.00 / 20.00 (price), 1200 / 1600 /
800 / 3200 / 600 (interval), 41000 / 43400 / 140 / 70 / 2600 (booked miles), 62000 / 61300 / 55 /
35 / 900 (host miles), 0.025 and 0.015 (valuation holdbacks, against real tiers of
0.05/0.02/0.08/0.04/0.06/0.03), 0.96 / 1.02 / 0.99 (class-move shares, against real tiers of
0.94/0.97/1.03/1.015/0.95/0.98). No factor is leaked into any baseline. Two small integers used
as hypothetical additions in the photograph and image baselines (5 and 2; 5, 2 and 1) coincide in
value with some addition tiers, but they do not match this or the other task's actual addition
set and reveal no factor's existence or identity; recorded as low-risk residue, not a defect.

## bijection_verdict

**PASS for task 0's domain**, with one policy-side note recorded below.

Every normative atom of `listings_ext_fault_intake`, `listings_ext_valuation_assessment`,
`listings_ext_class_assignment` and `listings_ext_price_reset`, of the base policies governing
their subjects, and of the six class variants those policies read, has a prose home whose meaning
is the same at the level of entailment. Every declared factor's ladder is carried in full, tier
by tier, with every limb of every compound condition, every threshold in figures, and — for the
method factors — the operation, operand, rounding mode and moment exactly as the source pins
them. Every baseline rule is carried complete in its own computation document with the policy's
own default constants rendered as figures. The three retired base clauses in scope are written as
retired and not as rules in force; nothing retired has vanished; the KB retires nothing the
source did not. All three prerequisite sentences stand verbatim, in their declared state form,
each in exactly one document of the policy it blocks, with the connective and the strength
unchanged, and each is resolvable at that strength from the sentence, the depended-on policy's
own rule and the records.

No `KB-BIJECTION RED` in task 0's domain.

**Policy-side note 1 — an enum argument that no rule decides.** `inspection_channel` on
`record_vehicle_valuation_559b4236` is a scored argument, and neither the source nor the KB
states a rule choosing among `self_photo` / `partner_shop` / `mobile_inspector` /
`telematics_report` for a marketplace-produced valuation. The GT value `mobile_inspector` is
recoverable only by copying the channel on the vehicle's own standing valuation. The documents
are faithful — they carry exactly the enum definition the tool contract gives and add no rule —
so this is an openness of the policy, not a translation defect. It is noted because the same
shape produces an actual divergence in task 1 (see that file), and because a scored argument
decided by no rule is worth the policy layer's attention.

**Policy-side note 2 — `lapsed_registration_image_addition_8c25d3d0` inherits a gap.** This
document belongs to task 1's domain and is analysed there; it is cross-referenced here only so
the difficulty's closing checklist is complete.

**Corpus-level cross-reference.** A `KB-BIJECTION RED` and a `KB-RUNTIME RED` are recorded in
task 1's files against `listings_ext_booked_consumption` and `listings_ext_reported_consumption`
— the two mileage policies, which are outside task 0's domain and do not affect any of task 0's
four scored values. The difficulty as a whole therefore does not close out on this round even
though task 0 passes all three parts.

## dependency_form

Scanned: the whole 77-document product corpus, against the blind answer's hop marks (all three of
task 0's hops were marked **state-derived**, none action-named, none pre-solved).

**Prerequisite sentences.** Each of the six sentences in the corpus (three of them task 0's)
appears exactly once, in a document of the policy it blocks, in its declared form. No state-form
sentence is restated anywhere as an action, and none names a performer, a resolving problem, a
tool, a policy id or another document. Sentence 3, for example, stops at "the value the
marketplace has settled on for it" and never says who settles it or with what.

**Tool names.** Each of the eight task tools is named in exactly one document — its own hub's
"Making the entry" block — and nowhere else. No blocked problem's documents name any other
problem's tool. No share finder is named as a step to take.

**Routes, chains and aggregations.** No document states an order between problems beyond a
prerequisite sentence, no document carries a dependency table, checklist, roadmap or complete
route, and no document strings several problems into a procedure or an ordered step list. A
targeted search for ordering language ("only after", "not counted before", "only once", "not
settled before", "must first", "waits on") over all 77 documents returns exactly the six
prerequisite sentences plus one sentence of base law in `inspection_clock_operation_6d5e7602`
("the vehicle returns only after a re-inspection passes"), which is the source's own base clause
rendered as the source has it and is therefore a policy-side matter, not a rendering addition.

**Wrong-versus-right contrasts and cross-problem examples.** None. The "Points of judgement" and
"worked reading" sections throughout contrast **boundary values of the same rule** (365 against
364 days, 12 against 11 images, exactly 5000 USD against 5000.01 USD) — which is a reading of one
rule, not a walk across problems. No FAQ or example demonstrates a chain, and none names a
mistake a solver might make about ordering.

**Factor documents.** None says which tier a customer, or most customers, fall on; none describes
"the reading a person without the rule would take"; none writes a task's evidence rows in as a
fact. Each states its ladder as a rule and leaves the tier to be derived from the records.

**Computation documents.** None hints that anything modifies it. No "unless otherwise provided",
no "adjustments may apply", no "certain customers qualify for", no "set out elsewhere", no
exception list, no pointer. The additive baselines do carry the source's own assembly sentence
("the additions the vehicle's record calls for are summed and applied once …"), which the render
contract requires to live in the baseline; it describes how additions combine and asserts that
any exists, names none, and points nowhere. No factor document names, overrides or points at a
computation document or another factor.

**Titles and openings.** All 77 titles name general subjects. The two `on_request` policies are
titled by the request type that defines them ("Setting the Daily Price a Host Asks", "The Host's
Own Periodic Odometer Reading"), which is that policy's general subject and not a task mirror. No
title or opening restates a customer request, labels a procedure for a specific situation, or
names a make, model, city, person or account state.

**Findability.** Every depended-on document in task 0's chain was reached in the blind audit
through the words the records and the prerequisite sentence use — "the vehicle value standing on
the listing", "a valuation … stands on the vehicle's condition record", "a fault … stands on that
record as a fault report of its own" — and not through phrasing borrowed from the dependent
document. Each cross-product factor document names the other product by its official name
(Keyturn Vehicle Care Plan, Keyturn Host Protection Plan, Keyturn Roadside Assistance) and the
kinds of records it reads, so it is reachable by a reader who has looked at those records.

**`KB-EXPLICIT: PASS` for task 0.**
